title: Haier vs. GE Dehumidifier (2026): Same Owner, Different Machines
dek: Haier owns GE Appliances, but their dehumidifiers aren't twins — and the differences in coverage and track record point one way.
description: Haier vs. GE dehumidifier, head to head: the 50-pint pump models compared on who builds them, rated coverage, pump lift, warranty and recall history.
intro: Shoppers compare Haier vs. GE dehumidifiers for an understandable reason: Haier has owned GE Appliances since 2016, so it's natural to assume the machines are the same underneath. They aren't, at least not in any way the companies have documented.

GE's current dehumidifiers are built under license by Midea, a relationship visible in ENERGY STAR's certification records. Haier's own-badged Smart Dry models (QDHR20LZ, QDHR35LZ, QDHR50LZ and the pump-equipped QPHR50LZ) share some branding and similar specs, but Haier doesn't disclose who builds them.

Below we compare each brand's closest model — a 50-pint unit with a built-in pump — on coverage, independent testing, warranty and recall history. Because the spec sheet and track record both point away from the Haier, our second pick is the closest pump model from outside the Haier family: Frigidaire's FHDP5033W1.
topPicksLead: For most buyers, the **GE 50-Pint with Pump** is the stronger choice: at the same 50 pints a day, GE rates it for up to 5,000 square feet — more than three times the Haier's figure — and its pump lifts water 15 feet through an included 16-foot hose.

products.name: GE 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump
pros: Rated for spaces up to 5,000 sq ft
Built-in pump lifts water 15 feet vertically
Smart Dry mode adjusts fan speed automatically
products.whyWeLoveIt: This GE pairs 50-pint capacity with a pump that pushes water up and out of a basement, and it ships with the 16-foot hose to do it. GE rates it for far more floor space than the Haier, and the controls cover what a basement unit needs: a humidistat, a 24-hour timer and Smart Dry fan control.
products.performance: GE rates it at 50 pints a day for basements, garages and large open spaces up to 5,000 square feet. The pump moves water up to 15 vertical feet to a sink or drain; if you'd rather not use it, the 15-pint bucket sounds a 10-second alarm when it's full or missing. The humidistat runs from 30% to 70%, Smart Dry nudges the fan speed up or down based on the humidity reading, and the washable filter needs no replacements. There's no app; GE's Wi-Fi 50-pint model adds Alexa and Google control but drops the pump. See the rest of the lineup in our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If neither Haier's conservative coverage rating nor GE's one-year warranty sits right with you, this Frigidaire is the closest match from outside the Haier family: the same 50-pint, pump-equipped format, with Wi-Fi scheduling and longer sealed-system coverage.
products.performance: Frigidaire rates the pump for 16.4 feet of vertical lift, enough to clear a basement window or reach a laundry sink. The spec sheet lists 545 watts and 49 dBA, and an operating range of 41–89°F at 30–80% relative humidity. Newer stock ships as the FHDP5033Y1, the same machine on R-32 refrigerant. More of the lineup is in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared each brand's published spec sheets and warranty terms, checked ENERGY STAR's certification records for manufacturer details, looked for independent test results on the current generation, and searched the CPSC recall database for both names. We also read owner reviews for recurring complaints.

sections.heading: Who actually builds Haier and GE dehumidifiers?

blocks.text: GE's answer is on the record: Midea builds GE's current dehumidifiers under license. Haier's isn't published. What stands out is the overlap — both brands use the same Smart Dry fan-speed name, and the pump models' bucket sizes, fan speeds and wattage are close enough to suggest a shared engineering platform. That's an inference, not a confirmed fact, so don't assume parts are interchangeable.

blocks.title: Ownership vs. manufacturing
blocks.text: Haier owns the GE Appliances business and licenses the GE name, but owning a brand doesn't mean building its products. For more on who makes what, see our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup.

sections.heading: Coverage and controls: where GE pulls ahead

blocks.text: The biggest spec gap is easy to miss. At the same 50 pints a day, Haier rates its unit for about 1,500 square feet while GE claims up to 5,000 — more than three times as much. Both figures come from each company's own spec sheets, so Haier is simply far more conservative. For a large basement, that matters; our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains how to match capacity to space.

On the pump itself, GE spells out the details: water lifts up to 15 vertical feet through a 16-foot hose that comes in the box, so you can reach a laundry sink or a basement window without buying extra parts. Neither brand's current pump model has an independent lab result we can tie to the exact unit sold, so the coverage rating, the documented manufacturer and the included hardware carry the comparison.

In 2021, the CPSC announced a recall of about 2 million dehumidifiers built by New Widetech and sold under 20 brand names, after 107 reported fire incidents and roughly $17 million in property damage. Older Haier models — HEN70ETFP, HEN70ETFP-E, HM50EP and HM70EP, made before September 1, 2017 — were included. Haier's current Smart Dry units aren't part of it, and GE's current Midea-built lineup isn't named.

If you're buying either brand secondhand, check the model number and manufacture date against the CPSC's recall list first. When an old unit reaches the end of its life, our [how to dispose of a dehumidifier](/guides/how-to-dispose-of-a-dehumidifier/) guide explains safe recycling.

items.label: Buy the GE 50-Pint with Pump if…
items.text: you're drying a large basement or garage, need water pumped up to a sink or window, and prefer a documented manufacturer. If you want app alerts instead and have a floor drain, GE's Wi-Fi 50-pint model trades the pump for Alexa and Google control.

items.label: Why we don't pick the Haier QPHR50LZ
items.text: Haier rates it for only about 1,500 sq ft at the same 50 pints, and there's no independent test of the current generation, so the GE is the better buy.

items.label: Buy the Frigidaire FHDP5033W1 if…
items.text: warranty matters most. Haier and GE both offer only one year; Frigidaire's five-year sealed-system coverage is longer, and this model adds Wi-Fi and a 16.4-ft pump lift. More in our [Midea vs. Frigidaire](/compare/midea-vs-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) comparison.

blocks.text: Haier owning GE Appliances doesn't make their dehumidifiers the same. The **GE 50-Pint with Pump** comes from GE's Midea-built lineup, is rated for more than three times the Haier's coverage, and includes a 16-foot hose with a 15-foot pump lift. The Haier QPHR50LZ is the more conservative machine on paper, and the spec sheet favors GE. Both carry one-year warranties, so if that's the sticking point, the **Frigidaire FHDP5033W1** offers a pump, Wi-Fi and five-year sealed-system coverage. Compare other pump-equipped options in our [dehumidifiers with a pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

faqs.a: Haier bought GE Appliances in 2016 and licenses the GE brand name. But GE's current dehumidifiers are built by Midea under license, not by Haier's own factories.

faqs.q: Which is better, a Haier or GE dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most buyers, GE. Its 50-pint pump model is rated for up to 5,000 square feet versus Haier's 1,500 at the same capacity, and it ships with a 16-foot hose and a 15-foot pump lift. GE also documents that Midea builds its dehumidifiers; Haier doesn't say who builds its own.

faqs.q: Are Haier and GE dehumidifiers the same?
faqs.a: Not officially. They share Smart Dry branding and similar specs, which hints at a common platform, but Haier doesn't disclose its manufacturer and no shared factory has been confirmed.
Neither. Both offer a one-year limited warranty on their current dehumidifiers. If warranty is the priority, Frigidaire's five-year sealed-system coverage is longer.

faqs.q: Have Haier or GE dehumidifiers been recalled?
faqs.a: Several older Haier models made before September 1, 2017, were part of the 2021 New Widetech recall. Haier's current Smart Dry units and GE's current lineup aren't included.
